correctness.rationale: The proof derives Hill scalar equation from the exact no-vertical linearization; Perron positivity and growth-rate inequalities force a positive periodic Riccati solution; periodic integration gives the exact variance defect and strictness. A pointwise Riccati extremum plus integrated Cauchy–Schwarz gives a uniform finite-amplitude sine penalty. The explicit sinusoid satisfies V positive and V prime +d V strictly positive and has a rigorously negative Floquet bound even though the averaged constant vector model has positive growth. Exact rational tests plus numerical corroboration in standalone checker.

value.rationale: Provides a concrete analytic local invasion-sign reversal under a smooth, demographically compatible seasonal population despite supercritical arithmetic-mean risk, an interpretable and model-motivated distinction relevant to periodic vector surveillance. Exact strict variance and nonperturbative quantitative bounds determine why a frozen/averaged risk index can be misleading; no general-policy or nonlinear-endemic claim is made.
